newsitem.title: USA: Vermont unemployment steadies at 3.9 pct in April.
newsitem.headline: Vermont unemployment steadies at 3.9 pct in April.

text.p: Vermont's unemployment rate steadied at 3.9 percent in April, and while government jobs have fluctuated in 1997, private sector employment has been almost flat, the state department of labor said on Tuesday.
April saw the recovery of 300 of the 400 jobs that were lost in March. The government sector rebounded, gaining 400 jobs after slipping by 500 in March.

While manufacturing lost 300 jobs, mostly in nondurable production, retail trade grew by 500 positions. Minor changes in other areas of the economy, however, caused a net loss of 100 jobs in private industry, the state department of labor said.
A detailed breakdown of the unseasonally adjusted data for Vermont's various labor markets follows:
--Barre-Montpelier, 4.6 pct, down from 5.0 pct in March, and 5.4 pct a year-ago.
--Bennington-Manchester, 4.0 pct, down from 4.4 pct in March and 5.5 pct a year-ago.
--Burlington, 2.8 pct, down from 2.9 pct in March and 3.0 pct a year-ago.
--Enosburg, 7.7 pct, down from 8.9 pct in March and 8.7 pct a year-ago.
--Hartford-Lebanon, VT-NH labor market, 2.1 pct, unchanged from March, down from 2.4 pct a year-ago.
--Keene-Brattleboro, VT labor market only, 4.2 pct, up from 3.1 pct in March but down from 5.2 pct a year-ago.
--Middlebury, 4.1 pct, down from 4.8 pct in March and 4.8 pct a year-ago.
--Morristown-Stowe, 6.2 pct, up from 5.8 pct in March but down from 7.9 pct in April.
--Newport, 8.8 pct, down from 9.5 pct in March and 9.2 pct a year-ago.
--Randolph, 3.9 pct, down from 4.0 pct in March and 4.3 pct a year-ago.
--Rutland, 4.4 pct, up from 4.3 pct in March but down from 5.5 pct a year-ago.
--St. Johnsbury, 5.5 pct, down from 5.9 pct in March and 6.6 pct a year-ago.
--Springfield, 5.1 pct, up from 4.4 pct in March but down from 6.2 pct a year-ago.
